saints.name: St. Fidelis of Sigmaringen
saints.title: Priest and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A lawyer turned Capuchin, the “advocate of the poor” who died preaching the faith to the Grisons…
biography: Born Mark Rey at Sigmaringen in 1577, the burgomaster's son, he studied at Freiburg, travelled France and Italy as a nobleman's tutor, and in 1611 took the doctorate in canon and civil law. An advocate who pleaded the cause of the poor without fee, he left the bar, sickened by the corruption of the courts.

Ordained priest in 1612, he entered the Capuchins at Freiburg, taking the name Fidelis. He served as guardian of the convents of Rheinfelden, Freiburg, and Feldkirch and won fame as a preacher against the Calvinism spreading through the Alpine valleys.

In 1621 he was sent to the Grisons, where Calvinism had taken root, and the new Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith made him mission superior. On 24 April 1622, after Mass at Grüsch, he was preaching at Seewis when an armed mob broke in; refusing apostasy, he answered, 'I came to extirpate heresy, not to embrace it', and was cut down.

The first martyr of Propaganda Fide, he was buried at Feldkirch, his head and arm kept at Chur. Beatified in 1729 and canonized by Benedict XIV in 1746, he is a patron of lawyers in memory of his first calling.
saints.knownFor: Dying as the first martyr of the missions of Propaganda Fide.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 24 April
